llm.summary: The skill is a clearly documented self-hosted speech-service helper, with sensitive network and staging behavior disclosed and aligned with its purpose.

dimensions.detail: Network access, local shell examples, GPU/container requirements, and large model/data storage are proportionate to a self-hosted speech service, with clear warnings about trusted endpoints, TLS, auth, and public exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses Docker images and model downloads with a bind-mounted data directory; this is coherent for the service, though operators should treat image provenance and the unpinned latest tags as normal deployment considerations.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to user-directed curl, Docker, ffmpeg, MCP, and file-staging workflows; the artifact includes explicit guardrails against browsing or deleting other callers' staged files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Server-side staged uploads, URL download cache, model files, and custom voice files persist under the Talkies data directory; persistence is disclosed, user-controlled, and paired with cleanup/auth guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill sends audio, transcript text, TTS input, and optional voice-cloning material to the configured Talkies service, which is central to ASR/TTS functionality and is repeatedly disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to send audio, text, and any voice samples to a Talkies server you run or trust. Enable bearer auth, prefer localhost or HTTPS, avoid debug logging with real data, clean up staged files, and do not use voice cloning without explicit speaker consent.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: The TTS curl examples transmit input text to TALKIES_URL, which is expected for the documented speech API and explicitly warned as data leaving the host.
[E1] expected: The custom voice example uses configured voice-cloning assets with the Talkies server; the artifact clearly states consent requirements and trusted-server expectations.
[E1] expected: General speech requests over curl create an external transmission boundary, but the artifact repeatedly scopes it to an operator-chosen endpoint and recommends auth and trusted deployments.
